system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In May 2026, Anucha entered an instalment agreement for a 240,000 baht debt payable in 24 instalments of 10,000 baht each. He defaulted on instalment 5 only; all other instalments were paid on time. On what amount may the creditor claim default interest? Answer briefly, stating the amount with a one-sentence reason.
raw_response:
**Applicable provision:** Section 224/1 of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code (inserted by the Civil and Commercial Code Amendment Act (No. 21), B.E. 2564 (2021), effective 11 April 2021), which governs default interest on debts payable by installments.

**Answer:** The creditor may claim default interest only on the **10,000 baht** corresponding to the defaulted 5th instalment.

**Reason:** Section 224/1 provides that where a debt is payable by instalments and the debtor defaults on one or more instalments but continues to pay the remaining instalments on time, the creditor may charge default interest only on the amount of the overdue instalment(s) actually in default — not on the entire outstanding principal — unless the debtor's default causes the whole debt to become due and demandable under a valid acceleration clause that has actually been invoked; since here only instalment 5 was missed and all others were paid on schedule, default interest attaches solely to that 10,000-baht instalment.
